points: Study led by University of Exeter (UK) analysed UK Biobank and US All of Us data, covering ~1 million individuals.

Parallel precedent: Rajendra Pal Gautam (AAP) faced similar backlash in 2022, later joined Congress.
Reflects Ambedkar's 'graded inequality' concept—OBCs ranked above Dalits despite shared backward status.

points: Houthis claimed a ballistic missile attack on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery (capacity 550,000 bpd) in Eastern Province.
Explosions also hit Riyadh; Saudi-led coalition intercepted missiles targeting the capital and Eastern Province.
Context: Houthi-Saudi conflict reignited July 2026, amid wider West Asia war between U.S. and Iran.
Houthis declared maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia, seized Red Sea coastline in September offensive.
Egypt's Parliament authorised defensive military support for Saudi Arabia; Houthis call it a declaration of war.
Saudi, Turkish, Pakistani officials visited Tehran to de-escalate; Riyadh-Ankara-Islamabad signed NATO-style Mecca defence pact.
Impacts global oil supply given Saudi Arabia's status as world's top crude exporter.

Demand: withdraw EPFO circular dated January 18, 2025, alleged to nullify Supreme Court order via executive action.
EPFO (Employees' Provident Fund Organisation) under Union Ministry of Labour & Employment is the body involved.
NCPA alleges bureaucratic delays, frivolous appeals against High Court judgments, and punitive interest penalties on pensioners.
Demand for time-bound mechanism and Joint Options acceptance without penalties for higher pension on higher wages.
Matters for social security rights of retirees and executive accountability vs judicial orders.

points: A.P. United Teachers' Federation demanded Old Pension Scheme implementation and protection of public education.
Protest held in Vijayawada under South Teachers' Federation of India banner.
Citing NITI Aayog report: ~90,000 primary schools closed/merged nationally; U-DISE Plus data: 972 AP primary schools unofficially closed in two years.
Government schools account for only 42% of students per the report cited.
Demands: 6% of GDP for education, 30% of State budget, teacher recruitment via TET/DSC within six months.
Highlights tension between public and private education and employee pension reform debate (OPS vs NPS).

Survey covered 201 Class 7 students in 20 schools that started English medium in 2019-20, with Deena Bandhu Trust, Chamarajanagar.
Assessed listening, speaking, reading, writing skills; found students can't narrate stories or form sentences.
KDA chairman Purushottama Bilimale argues mother-tongue education is the best model for foundational learning.
Recommendations: strengthen Kannada medium till Class 5, enhance role of State Educational Research and Training Dept.
Relevant to debate on medium of instruction policy under NEP 2020.

points: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra urged states to adopt prudent borrowing, better cash management for fiscal sustainability.
Statement made at 36th Conference of State Finance Secretaries in Mumbai, attended by 27 states, 3 UTs, CGA, CAG officials.
Urged states to onboard Unified Lending Interface (ULI) and use programmable CBDC (P-CBDC) for Direct Benefit Transfers.
Advised use of State Level Bankers' Committee (SLBC) forum for banking coordination.
RBI released 'Compendium on Cash and Debt Management for State Governments'.
Conference reviewed state market borrowings and Benchmark Issuance Strategy implementation.
Matters for state fiscal health, cooperative federalism in financial management.

Criticised multiple Benches being assigned same case categories, enabling 'manual intervention' in listing.
CJI is 'master of the roster' with administrative power to constitute Benches and allocate work.
Suggested High Court-style committee-based collective decision-making instead of CJI-centric system.
Supported collegium system but demanded more transparency in its functioning.
Matters for judicial accountability, transparency and institutional reform in the judiciary.

points: U.P. Cabinet approved PRAGATI Park, a robotics and AI hub, in Greater Noida over 69.52 acres.
PRAGATI = Platform for Robotics and AI Growth Through Technology and Innovation.
Expected to generate 1 lakh+ jobs and add ₹2,000 crore annually in GVA to state economy.
Zone 1 (8 acres): PPP model SPV with Greater Noida Authority holding 26% equity, private partner 74%.
Zone 2 (61.52 acres): private investment, no state capital liability.
State to give interest-free loan of ₹126.2 crore for 30 years; Authority to contribute ₹21.1 crore equity.
Reflects push for indigenous robotics manufacturing and state-level industrial policy/PPP investment models.

points: J&K police arrested Kashmiri Pandit activist Rakesh Handoo for circulating an 'edited terror threat' against Kashmiri Pandit employees in Kashmir valley.
Arrested by Baramulla police team on October 17; charged under IT Act Sections 66F (cyber terrorism) and 84C.
He allegedly altered electronic material from group 'Soldier of Resistance/United Liberation Council', falsely naming a complainant as target.
Complainant Rohit Raina, a Kashmiri Pandit employee whose name appeared in the threat list, filed the police complaint.
Handoo had earlier approached NHRC and NCM demanding probe into leak of personal data of Prime Minister Package Employees in Kashmir.
The original threat letter (circulated before Independence Day) forced extra security arrangements for Pandit employees.
Shows intersection of cyber law, internal security, and minority safety issues in J&K.

points: Cyclone Arnab approaching Andhra Pradesh coast; evacuations, train/flight cancellations, and cyclone shelters activated.

points: Very severe cyclonic storm Arnab made landfall on Andhra Pradesh coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, south of Yanam, on Oct 28, 2026.
Max sustained wind speed 125-135 kmph gusting to 150 kmph; landfall process started around 1.20 a.m.
IMD (India Meteorological Department) tracked and issued landfall updates; landfall near Yanam-Kakinada region.
Affected areas: Andhra Pradesh coastal districts, southern Odisha, north Chennai, Tiruvallur (storm surge/high waves).
One death reported in Visakhapatnam due to live electrical wires; 206 trees uprooted there.
Relief camps set up in Yanam (Puducherry enclave) for ~5,000 people; NDRF and local police deployed to persuade residents to evacuate.
Civil Aviation Ministry held review meeting; flights cancelled at Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada airports due to disruption.

Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei disclosed a letter from US VP J.D. Vance seeking to revive talks.
Qatari delegation visited Tehran for talks, showing mediation efforts are active.

ILO defines 'decent work' as employment offering equitable income, workplace rights, social security and dignity.
SDG-8 (Sustainable Development Goal) advocates 'decent work for all' - India's labour market shows high informality.

Wind speeds of 100-110 kmph, gusting to 120 kmph forecast; IMD classifies it as Severe Cyclonic Storm.
Orange alert in six Telangana districts, yellow alert in five; schools/colleges closed in Chennai, Tiruvallur districts.
NDRF deployed 6 teams, SDRF 7 teams in Andhra Pradesh; APSDMA coordinating response, landfall point likely Ongole.
Chennai recorded rainfall across stations (Ennore Port highest at 39mm); AP CM sought TN assistance for power restoration.

points: Madras High Court ruled litigants not entitled to refund of court fees if out-of-court settlement happens after trial commences.
Justice P.B. Balaji refused to follow SC's 2021 M.C. Subramaniam judgment, instead followed SC's 2010 Afcons Infrastructure case (co-equal bench binding).
Tamil Nadu Court Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1955 governs refund; Section 69 (50% refund) and Section 69A (100% refund for ADR referral) are key provisions.
SC's Afcons ruling held civil courts can refer disputes to ADR (Section 89 CPC) only before trial commencement.
Judicial principle reaffirmed: later bench of equal strength must refer to larger bench if disagreeing, not take contrary view directly.
Matters for litigants and State exchequer - affects incentive structure for early settlement via ADR mechanisms.

Avarekai widely grown in Bengaluru Rural, Magadi, Ramanagara, Chickballapur, Kolar, Mysuru, Mandya; consumed Nov-Feb.
UAS-Bengaluru (GKVK) developed improved Hebbal Avare varieties (HA 3, HA 4, HA 5) for year-round cultivation.

Federal Election Assistance Commission (EAC) only certifies voting machines/trains staff; actual conduct done by thousands of county officials across 50 states.

points: UNGA resolution titled 'Necessity of ending the economic, commercial and financial embargo imposed by USA against Cuba' passed on October 30.

Several Latin American countries (Costa Rica, Ecuador, Argentina, Colombia) switched votes after downgrading ties with Havana.
Germany and Italy abstained for the first time, citing Cuba-Russia ties and Russia-Ukraine war.
India maintained support for the resolution, calling for 'dialogue and diplomacy'.
BRICS New Delhi declaration earlier expressed 'deep concern' over the US blockade's humanitarian impact on Cuba.

Iotova set to become first elected woman president in Bulgaria (population 6.4 million).

points: Madras High Court Advocates Association (MHAA) filed PIL challenging 1965 Union Cabinet decision continuing English as common language for Supreme Court and all High Courts.

MHAA learnt of the 1965 decision only in 2025 via an RTI Act, 2005 application.
Centre had earlier rejected Tamil Nadu's proposals (2006, 2014) to use Tamil in Madras High Court proceedings.

points: Sri Lanka's national power grid collapsed on October 17, causing blackout for over 5 hours affecting 23 million people.

Grid frequency fell from 49.906 Hz to 48.75 Hz within two seconds after Lakvijaya coal plant output dropped sharply.
Under Frequency Load Shedding (UFLS) scheme failed to prevent total system collapse; similar rooftop solar-related issue flagged in Feb 2025 blackout too.
Relevant for India as its rooftop solar capacity stands at 33.41 GW, needing similar grid stability safeguards.

points: India has had decades of persistently high anaemia prevalence in women and children.

IFA is a targeted/precision strategy for vulnerable groups; fortification is a broad, population-wide strategy.

National surveys show iron deficiency is NOT the major cause of anaemia in India; one-third of cases show no micronutrient deficiency at all.
Key issue: whether dietary iron intake is actually inadequate, and whether supplemented iron is properly absorbed/utilised.
Policy shift needed towards dietary diversification rather than only pills/fortification for sustainable anaemia reduction.
